# `ext::https_server` — declaration reference

Generated source inventory. Linked guides own runtime and semantic contracts; a listed declaration does not establish executable behavior.

[All modules](../README.md) · [Source](../../../extended/ext/https_server.lani#L3)

Layer: `ext`. Role: module. Profile: **Source inventory**.

Shared server Protocol over OpenSSL 3 on Linux x86_64/glibc. Thirty-four direct native cases across seven groups pass through separate receipts: six verified steps, two early closures, four fatal-preparation/abort cleanup, four normal-close cleanup, six constructor/quota, four constructor-allocation and eight paired TLS 1.2/1.3 teardown cases. The teardown receipt is 21.05 seconds and checks missing-alert timeout, a cut native record, drain-cap overflow, authenticated empty input, pre-exit release and sticky replay. Cleanup groups each reach two close EIO injections; constructor allocation reaches three dynamic source failures, excluding native OpenSSL heap allocations. begin_connected consumes its accepted nonblocking socket on entry/error and eagerly creates a Session while ServerContext is borrowed; SSL_new retains the native reference. Steps never poll and perform zero or one active TLS attempt. HTTP events require verified handshake policy, stable writes survive WANT, and both protocol versions require local notify plus bounded discard to authenticated peer EOF before terminal publication. The raw 12-case closure experiment is distinct lower-layer evidence. SIGPIPE policy and manual ownership remain explicit; cryptography stays in OpenSSL. Rare WANT schedules and clock failures after native calls retain finite coverage gaps.
